Question 10(d) [12 marks]: What does art reveal about society in Minoan Crete during this period? Support your response using evidence from relevant sources.

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 12):
10–12 marks: Provides an informed explanation of what art reveals about society during this period | Demonstrates detailed knowledge and understanding relevant to the question | Integrates evidence from a range of relevant sources to support the response | Communicates effectively using a range of appropriate historical terms and concepts
7–9 marks: Provides an explanation of what art reveals about society during this period | Demonstrates knowledge and understanding relevant to the question | Uses evidence from a range of relevant sources to support the response | Communicates using appropriate terms and concepts
4–6 marks: Provides some understanding of what art reveals about society | Demonstrates some knowledge relevant to the question | Refers to one or more sources in the response | Communicates using some appropriate historical terms and concepts
1–3 marks: Makes general statement(s) about society/an aspect of society | May refer to source(s) | May use historical terms and/or concepts


ANSWERS COULD INCLUDE (the student does not need every point):
• Art reveals information about religion, clothing and leisure. Frescoes show women dancing and gathering crops, as well as attending feasts and riding in carriages. There are also scenes of hunting.
• Bull leaping is depicted in art including sculpture and frescoes, however archaeologists are uncertain whether this was a leisure or religious activity.
• Art also provides evidence of housing, frescoes and ceramic tiles show housing in the towns, eg Gournia.
• Seals in various materials including metal, stone, even crystal, show Minoan religious beliefs, including priestesses and connection to nature.
• Seals also indicate trade depicting economic activity.
• Frescoes depict women’s hairstyles and clothing, including cropped open jackets and colourful flounced skirts.
• Food is also depicted, for example in the Camp Stool Fresco, women are presented with glasses and jugs of wine, as well as food.
• Art reveals ceremonial and ritual scenes. The Tree and Sacred Grove Fresco shows women dancing and people watching which may show a kind of religious activity.
